'''Inter-Con Security Systems, Inc.''' is an American [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[Private security company|security services]] company headquartered in [[Pasadena, California]]. Inter-Con is one of the largest [[private security companies]] in the world with over 40,000 employees<ref name="history" /> across North America, South America and Africa. The company offers security personnel and management, executive protection programs, risk assessments, tactical exercise plans and programs, emergency medical services, classified information safeguarding and investigations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Inter-Con Security Systems Inc |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/0123407D:US |website=Bloomberg |publisher=Bloomberg}}</ref>

==History==
Inter-Con Security Systems, Inc. was founded in 1973 with the goal of developing and implementing comprehensive security programs custom tailored to its clients' needs. Retired [[Los Angeles Police Department|Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD)]] Detective Enrique "Hank" Hernandez and his wife Bertha Hernandez founded Inter-Con in [[Alhambra, California]] in 1973. Since 1986, his son, [[Enrique Hernandez, Jr.]], has been president and [[Chief executive officer|Chief Executive Officer]].<ref>{{cite news |date=26 August 2017 |title=How Wells Fargo Bought Millions in Services From an Independent Director's Firm |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/video-wells-fargo-bought-millions-202400145.html |publisher=Yahoo! Finance}}</ref> It remains a privately owned company.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wells Fargo - Board of Directors - Enrique Hernandez |url=https://www.wellsfargo.com/about/corporate/boardofdirectors/hernandez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623211246/https://www.wellsfargo.com/about/corporate/boardofdirectors/hernandez |archive-date=2015-06-23 |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=www.wellsfargo.com}}</ref>

The company's first customer was the [[NASA|U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)]] to implement a security program incorporating a variety of security disciplines in a classified environment. <ref>{{cite web |title=About Us |url=https://www.icsecurity.com/about-us/ |publisher=Inter-Con Security Systems}}</ref>

In March 2025, the [[United States Institute of Peace]] (USIP) cancelled a contract with Inter-Con amidst a dispute with the [[Department of Government Efficiency]] (DOGE). USIP was concerned that Inter-Con would allow DOGE members access to the [[United States Institute of Peace Headquarters|USIP headquarters]], as Inter-Con's federal contracts could be leveraged to force their cooperation with DOGE.  After the contract was cancelled, Inter-Con staff used a physical key that had been issued and not returned to assist DOGE personnel in entering the building and seizing USIP security personnel and weapons.<ref>{{cite web |date=18 March 2025 |title=DOGE plays hardball in U.S. Institute of Peace takeover |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2025/03/18/doge-institute-of-peace-takeover-musk-trump/ |work=The Washington Post}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=20 March 2025 |title=DOGE Strong-Armed USIP Security Contractors to Switch Sides |url=https://talkingpointsmemo.com/edblog/breaking-doge-strong-armed-usip-security-contractors-to-switch-sides |work=Talking Points Memo}}</ref>  According to sworn testimony from USIP head of security Colin O'Brien, "DOGE threatened to cancel every federal contract Inter-Con held" if they did not assist DOGE in accessing their former client's premises.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BREAKING: DOGE Strong-Armed USIP Security Contractors to Switch Sides |url=https://talkingpointsmemo.com/edblog/breaking-doge-strong-armed-usip-security-contractors-to-switch-sides |access-date=2025-03-19 |website=TPM – Talking Points Memo |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Operations==
Inter-Con's security services include physical security, program management, electronic security, security consulting and training, specialized services, active shooter response, and executive protection.<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Services |url=https://www.icsecurity.com/our-services/ |publisher=Inter-Con Security Systems}}</ref> The company's client list includes federal, state and local governments, multinational corporations, non-governmental organizations, public utilities, private businesses, hospitals, sports arenas, and high net worth individuals, among others.<ref>{{cite news |date=18 June 2009 |title=Border Companies Thrive on Mexican-Americans |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/06/18/business/smallbusiness/18edge.html |work=New York Times}}</ref> Internationally, Inter-Con is a provider of diplomatic security services, safeguarding United States Embassies, as well as other embassy locations around the world.<ref>{{cite web |title=About Us |url=https://www.icsecurity.com/about-us/ |publisher=Inter-Con Security Systems}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Our Force at the Front Door |url=https://2001-2009.state.gov/m/ds/rls/33914.htm |publisher=U.S. Department of State}}</ref>

Key sectors served by Inter-Con include aerospace & defense, consumer goods & services, education, energy & utilities, financial, government & diplomatic, healthcare, manufacturing, natural materials & resources, and non-governmental organizations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sectors We Serve |url=https://www.icsecurity.com/sectors-we-serve/ |publisher=Inter-Con Security Systems}}</ref>

{{As of|2026}}, notable Inter-Con clients include the U.S. government,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tahiri |first=Damir |date=2023-04-04 |title=Inter-Con Wins Exclusive Security Contract for U.S. Embassy Tunisia |url=https://icsecurity.com/u-s-embassy-tunisia-awards-private-security-contract-to-inter-con/ |access-date=2026-07-12 |website=Inter-Con Security |language=en-US}}</ref> [[General Motors]],<ref>{{cite web |date=2025-02-21 |title=Inter-Con Security Awarded Entire U.S. Security Contract for General Motors |url=https://www.icsecurity.com/inter-con-security-awarded-entire-u-s-security-contract-for-general-motors/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223112029/https://www.icsecurity.com/inter-con-security-awarded-entire-u-s-security-contract-for-general-motors/ |archive-date=2025-02-23 |website=[[Inter-Con Security]]}}</ref> [[Ford Motor Company]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=InterCon Security Services and Ford Motor Company {{!}} National Labor Relations Board |url=https://www.nlrb.gov/case/07-CA-383866 |access-date=2026-07-12 |website=www.nlrb.gov}}</ref> and [[Cargill]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-11 |title=Business Item: 2025-168 |url=https://metrocouncil.org/Council-Meetings/Committees/Metropolitan-Council/2025/08-27-25/2025-168-Business-Item.aspx |website=[[Metropolitan Council (Minnesota)|Metropolitan Council]]}}</ref>
